title: Terraform-driven Upgrade Conductor with Health Sweeps for Private Control Plane
creator: Lena Park
description: Build a Terraform-first upgrade conductor that orchestrates private control plane version promotions across tenant VPCs. The conductor will invoke IaC workflows (Terraform workspaces and module versions), coordinate phased canary waves, run automated health sweeps (synthetic probes + telemetry gates), and perform automated rollbacks or pause-and-alert when safety gates fail. This ticket includes module design, orchestration API, and integration tests with the private control plane operator.
acceptance_criteria: A Terraform module (redwood/upgrade_conductor) exists that can: plan, apply, and taint only the control-plane components for a specified tenant without touching data plane workloads
The upgrade conductor can execute a configurable 3-wave canary promotion: small initial cohort, expanded cohort, and full promotion with pause windows between waves
Health sweep service evaluates: kube-level readiness, API latency P95, control-plane error-rate (5xx), and synthetic end-to-end smoke test; gates prevent promotion on violation
Automated rollback is triggered and documented when any gate trips during a wave; rollback is performed via Terraform apply to the previous version state
End-to-end integration tests run in CI (staging VPCs) and pass consistently; PRs include test harness and example workspace
Runbook created: manual override, emergency rollback steps, and monitoring dashboard links
design_notes: Use a thin orchestration service (upgrade-conductor) that calls out to Terraform Cloud/Enterprise API or self-hosted Terraform runner in customer VPCs
Represent control plane version as a module input (controlplane_image_tag / operator_version) and keep a compatibility matrix in the module
Wave membership determined by tenant tag / cohort label stored in the tenant registry; conductor evaluates tenant health baseline prior to upgrading
Health sweeps combine metrics (Prometheus), traces (Jaeger), and synthetic probes (kube exec + curl) executed from the same region as the tenant VPC
To limit blast radius, the conductor must support a dry-run mode, partial apply targeting, and canary isolation via provisioning replacement controlplane nodes in parallel to minimize downtime
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype terraform module and example workspace for one staging tenant (branch: feat/upgrade-conductor-terraform)
2) Build upgrade-conductor service with API to kick off waves and inspect plan outputs (go service + SDK wrapper for terraform)
3) Implement health-sweep adapters (prometheus query, api probe, smoke runner) and gate logic
4) Add automated rollback flow tied to terraform state snapshots and documented rollback job
5) CI: add integration test job that runs conductor against ephemeral staging VPCs, validate metrics and rollback behavior
6) Run internal pilot with 5 tenants, iterate on thresholds and add UI hooks in Console for manual hold/override
monitoring_and_rollbacks: Primary gates: controlplane_p95_latency < 250ms, controlplane_error_rate < 0.5% over 5m, synthetic_smoke_success == true
If any gate trips during a wave: mark wave as failed, run terraform apply to previous state snapshot, notify on-call via PagerDuty, open incident in Statuspage
Operator-level crashes detected => immediate pause, capture operator logs and kube events to S3, attach to incident
Conductor emits structured events to event-sink (kafka) for auditing and for Console rollout timeline
